IT Operations Engineer, Entry Level
IT Operations - New York, New York
IT Operations Engineer, Entry Level
Contract Opportunity, 6 Months- 5 days in the office
Position Summary
Hiring an entry-level engineer on a 6-month contract to own our inbound IT operations queue, shrink it and automate it. The job has two parts, and the second part is the real deliverable. First you work the queue: triage and resolve inbound tickets across the environment: account and access requests, licensing, phone and laptop provisioning, offboarding, and the long tail of “something isn’t working.” The second part is to automate what repeats: take the categories your own data says arrive most often, script them end to end, and hand the automation over with documentation so it keeps running after you.
This is an entry-level operations job. You will reset accounts and fix Microsoft Office problems. The difference is that here, doing a task by hand for the second or third time should be done via automation. You will leave with production automation you built, shipped, and handed over.
How We Work, and Who Does Well Here
Read this section before the requirements. It is the actual filter.
Scripting over click-ops. We call this a DevOps-track role because we want someone who believes repetitive work should be automated, even before they have all the skills to do it. The skills are learnable; the reflex mostly isn’t. If you have ever scripted something nobody asked you to, tell us about it.
We hire for how you work and learn, not what you already know. At entry level we assume you know almost none of our stack, but expect you to learn quickly.
Broad knowledge is expected. In one week this queue touches Microsoft 365, AWS, identity and access, phones, laptops, and monitoring alerts.
Writing is part of the job. Your first two weeks are spent shadowing each member of the team. Every ticket category you automate later ships with documentation.
You sit in the New York office with the team and the developers, full time. A large part of this job is being the person colleagues actually want to bring a problem to — responsive, honest about timelines, and clear about what you did and why.
Modern tooling, including AI. We use agentic AI tools (Claude Code) as a normal part of operations work, including for building the kind of automation this role delivers. You should be curious about working that way.
Key Responsibilities
Own day-to-day triage and resolution of the inbound ticket queue, with escalation paths to the rest of the team for what you cannot yet resolve.
Keep a running classification of everything that arrives — the data that decides what gets automated.
Build and ship automation for the highest-frequency categories, each with documentation and a handover. Examples from our own recent work:
license assignment and reclaim
account provisioning
offboarding
Write and maintain runbooks, and improve every procedure you touch.
Required Qualifications
0–2 years of experience. A degree is welcome but not required; a home lab, a help-desk stint, a repository of scripts, or a good story about a problem you automated at work all count as evidence.
Some exposure to scripting in any language — PowerShell, Python, bash, it does not matter which.
Care and accuracy with access and identity work. At a financial-services company, being careful matters more than being fast.
Clear written communication and the habit of closing the loop: tickets updated, requesters told, runbooks amended.
Willingness to learn our stack on the job. We use Microsoft 365 and Entra, AWS, Jira, Duo, Jamf, bash, PowerShell, TypeScript, CDK, Git and Claude Code. You are not expected to know these on day one; you are expected to be visibly learning them by week three.
Desired Attributes
Genuine curiosity about how systems fit together.
The instinct to notice when something has been done by hand too many times.
Reliability with the unglamorous half of the work, on the days when nothing is ready to be automated yet.

Your background, perspective, and desire to make an impact set you apart. As we work to help St. Jude cure childhood cancer, we're calling on the game-changers, innovators and visionaries to join our family. Not just for the kids of St. Jude, but also for you. Job Description
Responsible for providing technical leadership while actively engaging in the design, development, implementation, and support of multi-layered enterprise applications. This includes not only performing the appropriate software development lifecycle activities but also serving as a technical leader and mentor to other engineers. Serves as a subject matter expert in one or more aspects of software engineering best practices, which includes but is not limited to front-end UI & UX, APIs & microservices, schema development, and SecDevOps. Explores emerging technologies and anticipates industry disruptions. Documents and demonstrates solutions by developing documentation, flowcharts, layouts, diagrams, charts, code comments, and conforming to coding standards.
This role will support the design, development, and integration of customer data solutions leveraging Salesforce Data Cloud and related enterprise technologies to enable customer insights, data-driven engagement, and scalable data services across the organization.
Essential Job Functions
Responsible for technical analysis, design, and development of complex changes or project milestones across multiple systems within a platform, including troubleshooting, containment, issue resolution, and root cause analysis.
Lead and execute technical initiatives that may span multiple systems and applications.
Serve as a mentor to Software Engineers I and II, including assisting and training on technical and data analysis, problem solving, and code reviews to strengthen team capabilities.
Proactively engage with stakeholders through interviews and other information-gathering activities to support the development and enhancement of applications and services.
Maintain technical expertise by studying emerging development tools, programming techniques, and technologies while participating in educational opportunities.
Partner with business analysts and customers to resolve issues and plan for future business and technology needs.
Collaborate with users to understand system utilization and identify enhancement and modification opportunities.
Utilize technical and analytical expertise to analyze, design, and develop new application solutions.
Create, modify, test, debug, document, and maintain complex application programs.
Act as a lead resource for Software Engineers I and II by providing guidance, training, and mentorship throughout the Software Development Life Cycle.
Knowledge & Experience
Demonstrable knowledge of current application development techniques, including object-oriented and client/server technologies.
Professional experience developing software across multiple layers of the application stack, including front-end, back-end, data, and database technologies.
Experience working in a collaborative, cross-functional environment with defined structures, roles, and responsibilities.
Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Engineering, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related field, and 5-8 years of technical, analytical, systems, and programming experience.
Preferred Experience
Salesforce Data Cloud, including Unified Customer Profiles, Data Model Objects (DMOs), Data Graphs, and Calculated Insights.
Designing, developing, and supporting Customer Data Platform (CDP) solutions, customer identity resolution, and customer data unification strategies.
Audience segmentation, customer activation, and data-driven marketing technologies.
Event-streaming, messaging, and integration technologies, such as Kafka.
Modern cloud data architectures, including federated data access and zero-copy data sharing models.
Building scalable customer data solutions that support analytics, personalization, and customer engagement initiatives.
Applying data governance, privacy, security, and compliance best practices for customer and enterprise data.
Experience integrating Salesforce platforms with enterprise applications, APIs, and cloud-based data ecosystems.
